moments.title: Construction begins
moments.text: Sears, Roebuck and Co. broke ground for a new headquarters on Wacker Dr. SOM's Bruce Graham and engineer Fazlur Khan designed it as nine steel tubes bundled together.

moments.title: Topped out
moments.text: The last steel went up, and at about 1,450 feet and 108 stories it became the tallest building in the world.

moments.title: The Skydeck opens
moments.text: An observation deck opened on the 103rd floor, about 1,353 feet above the street.

moments.title: No longer the world's tallest
moments.text: The Petronas Towers in Kuala Lumpur took the world height title, which Sears Tower had held for about 25 years.

moments.title: Renamed Willis Tower; the Ledge opens
moments.text: The tower took the name of insurance broker Willis Group. The same month, glass boxes called the Ledge opened, jutting out from the Skydeck over Wacker Dr.

moments.title: A new base: Catalog
moments.text: A renovation added Catalog, a shopping and dining space at the base whose name nods to the Sears catalog. The Skydeck was redesigned and reopened in 2021.

moments.title: Today: Willis Tower and the Skydeck
moments.text: It is still the tallest building in Chicago and one of the tallest in the U.S., with offices and the Skydeck on the 103rd floor.

facts.label: Height
facts.note: Sources give 1,450 or 1,451 feet to the roof.

facts.label: Stories
facts.note: Some counts give 110, including mechanical floors.

sources.title: Willis Tower History and Facts (Skydeck Chicago)
The Forgotten History of Chicago Supertalls: Willis Tower (SOM)

checked.notes: Groundbreaking Aug 1970, topping out May 3, 1973, 108 stories, world's tallest until 1998, renamed July 2009, Ledge July 2009 and Skydeck on the 103rd floor confirmed (Skydeck Chicago, SOM, Britannica). Height is 1,450 or 1,451 feet depending on source; the story keeps 1,450. Catalog renovation scheduled for mid-2020; Skydeck reopened spring 2021. Skydeck Chicago bills it as the tallest building in Chicago.
